summary: Sierra Club, NRDC, Sustainable FERC Project, regional clean energy groups and two community organizations protest MISO's LARS filing as a permanent parallel process that shifts costs to other customers and DPP generators, discriminates, and departs from the show cause order's proximity test.
ask: Reject all of LARS and direct MISO to work with stakeholders on a different proposal; alternatively issue a deficiency letter, or at least delay effectiveness until MISO files its promised cost provisions.

points.point: The groups say LARS is a new permanent parallel process that shifts costs, creates reliability concerns and allows discrimination.
points.quote: MISO's LARS proposal is a new, permanent parallel interconnection study process that will shift costs from large loads to other existing and future transmission customers and resource owners

points.point: They note MISO's own account that LARS adopts no cost allocation methodology and defers cost shifting to later filings.
points.quote: LARS adopts no cost allocation methodology

points.point: Load-study and common violations go to Baseline Reliability or Other projects paid by all loads in the pricing zone, while DPP generators fund their own upgrades.
points.quote: LARS, therefore, takes a category of costs usually assigned to generators and assigns them to existing load.

points.point: They argue the standing injection persists after the paired load leaves, and zonal customers bear the cost.
points.quote: LARS creates a standing injection that was studied only on the assumption of a matched withdrawal

points.point: They say LARS would give a limited number of projects preferential access each year, with vertically integrated utilities deciding which.
points.quote: LARS sets up a generation and load study process that would offer a limited number of projects preferential access to the transmission system each year, year after year.

points.point: They say MISO invented an expansive definition of proximate instead of following the order's substation test.
points.quote: MISO invents a new expansive definition of "proximate" in an attempt to demonstrate that its proposal is responsive to the Commission's Order.

points.point: They argue siloed parallel processes raise upgrade costs and bias risk and favor integrated planning such as GALIP.
points.quote: meeting every new need with a new, siloed interconnection process (as MISO has done with ERAS, the ZGIA, now LARS, and soon the LLPR) significantly increases network upgrade costs

throughLine.text: Protests MISO's LARS filing against the E-8 show cause order's cost-shifting concern and its definition of electrically proximate large load, and notes the cost recovery agreement is deferred.

figures.label: Transmission investment approved in MTEP26, per the protest
figures.quote: approximately $14.7 billion of transmission investment approved in that cycle
